title: Preflight Runway: 30m QBR Checklist and Facilitation Lanes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact (30 minute) QBR template intended for customers with low-to-medium complexity contracts or for a mid-quarter sync focused on renewal signals, product adoption blockers, and a single prioritized success initiative. Use when stakeholders prefer short, action-oriented reviews rather than the full quarterly playbook.

Core principles (keep top of mind):
- Timebox tightly: every minute should surface a decision or a next-step owner.
- Facilitation lanes: assign conversational lanes (Business, Tech, Adoption, Renewal) to avoid rabbit holes.
- Signal-focused: prioritize measurable signals over long narrative slides.
- Clear outcomes: leave with up to 3 concrete follow-ups and owners.

30m micro-QBR agenda (timeboxed)
- 0:00–02:00 — Quick welcome & outcomes: facilitator sets the goal for the 30m. (Script: “Goal for this 30 minutes: surface renewal posture, confirm one adoption blocker we will solve, and agree on next steps.”)
- 02:00–08:00 — Topline health snapshot (owner: AM, 6m)
  - Usage trend (last 30d vs prior 30d): active seats, API calls, embeddings units.
  - Key wins / releases customer used.
- 08:00–18:00 — Signal triage (owner: CSM, 10m) — structured by facilitation lanes
  - Business lane (Facilitator prompt: “Any contract or stakeholder changes?”) — 2m
  - Tech lane (Facilitator prompt: “Any latency/cost/infra regressions or blockers?”) — 3m
  - Adoption lane (Facilitator prompt: “Are we shipping the promised pilot features? Blocking tasks?”) — 3m
  - Renewal lane (Facilitator prompt: “How would you rate renewal confidence? Any changes?”) — 2m
- 18:00–26:00 — Root-cause & immediate mitigation (owner: Solutions eng or AM, 8m)
  - Pick 1 highest-risk finding from Signal triage. Capture root cause hypothesis and one mitigation to run in the next 2 weeks.
- 26:00–29:00 — Commitments & owners (owner: facilitator, 3m)
  - 3 follow-ups max: owner, deliverable, due date (YYYY-MM-DD).
- 29:00–30:00 — Close and next meeting cadence (owner: AM, 1m)

Facilitation lanes (how to run them)
- Business lane (owner: AM) — quick check on org changes, procurement, PO priorities, go/no-go decisions. Escalation trigger: new procurement delays >14 days.
- Tech lane (owner: Solutions Eng or Tech Lead) — quick operational health: errors, latency, rate limits, private deployment alerts. Escalation trigger: production errors affecting >5% of calls or >3% increase in median latency.
- Adoption lane (owner: CSM) — feature usage, onboarding tasks, internal champions. Escalation trigger: champion replaced and no new champion identified within 10 business days.
- Renewal lane (owner: CSM/AM) — renewal sentiment, legal terms, budget windows. Escalation trigger: customer indicates budget re-prioritization or paused procurement.

Pre-meeting TO-DOS (2–5 business days before)
- CSM: run the 30d usage export and attach top 3 graphs (active seats, token usage, embed units).
- AM: confirm attendee list (must include technical and business stakeholder if possible).
- Solutions Eng: validate no open high-sev tickets; if present, brief mitigation plan for the meeting.
- Facilitator: send 10–15 second agenda email, attach 1-page snapshot (see "one-pager" template below).

One-pager snapshot (1 page, must be attached to invite)
- Topline line: Renewal confidence (High / Medium / Low) + primary risk (one-liner)
- 3 key metrics: last-30d % change vs prior 30d (active seats, API calls, error rate)
- Open blockers (1–3) with owners and current status
- Top ask from vendor (what we need from customer this week)

Facilitator scripts (brevity matters)
- Opening: “Thanks everyone — we’ll keep this to 30 minutes. By the end we’ll have a single prioritized action list to reduce renewal risk and unblock adoption.”
- When a lane veers long: “This is important but out of scope for this 30m; let’s park it in a follow-up and assign an owner.” (Use the parking-lot doc link.)
- If sentiment is unclear: quick poll: “On a scale of 1–5, how confident are you about renewing?” Capture responses privately if a stakeholder would prefer.

Minute-taking template (fill during meeting)
- Date:
- Attendees:
- Topline health summary (1 sentence):
- Signal selected for RCA:
- Root cause hypothesis (1 line):
- Action 1: owner / deliverable / due
- Action 2: owner / deliverable / due
- Action 3: owner / deliverable / due

Mini renewal-risk scoring (use during Signal triage)
- Score components (0–2 each): Usage downgrade (2), Exec sponsorship shift (2), Critical bug/regression (2), Budget timing mismatch (2).
- 0–1: Low risk, 2–4: Medium, 5–8: High.

Example follow-up tracker (paste into spreadsheet or sheet)
- columns: [action, owner, due_date, priority(one word), status(one word), context_link]
- example row: ["Deploy rate-limit tweak to reduce latency", "Ethan Cross", "2025-12-09", "High", "in_progress", "JIRA-CS-892"]

Pre-written meeting invite blurb (copy-paste)
Hi <Name>,
Quick 30-minute sync to review product health and align on the renewal runway. Attached: 1-page snapshot. Goal: confirm renewal posture, select one adoption blocker to fix, and agree next steps.
Agenda: 1) Topline health 2) Signal triage (business/tech/adoption/renewal lanes) 3) Mitigation & commitments
If you want more time for a technical deep-dive, we can schedule a follow-up.
Thanks,
<CSM name>

Post-meeting follow-up (within 48h)
- Facilitator: send meeting notes + actions (use minute-taking template) and mark owners in shared tracker.
- AM: if renewal sentiment is medium/low, schedule renewal prep meeting and escalate to Sales lead.
- Solutions Eng: open any new Jira tickets with priority and link to tracker.

Common pitfalls and mitigation patterns (bullet form)
- Pitfall: Meeting becomes a product roadmap debate — Mitigation: park roadmap requests and request product intake ticket.
- Pitfall: Only operational stakeholders attend — Mitigation: insist on a business sponsor for renewal conversations.
- Pitfall: No measurable metrics — Mitigation: require at least one usage metric attached to the one-pager or postpone.

Where to store artifacts
- Always attach the 1-page snapshot to the calendar invite and store minutes in the shared CS QBR folder. Tag with the account name and YYYY-MM-DD.

Quick variants (pick one if needed)
- 45m resilience QBR: add a 15m technical deep-dive after minute 26.
- 15m pulse check: skip RCA; only confirm Topline health and 1 immediate ask.

Notes / working items for improvement (TODOs)
- Build a calendar invite template in the CS playbooks doc library and automate the one-pager insertion.
- Add a small Loom capture for how to run Facilitation Lanes for new CSMs.

Document history and context:
- Origin: condensed playbook pulled from longer QBR template to support faster renewals for mid-market customers.
